changes: Place of copying set to empty: the colophon does not say where the copy was made. 'bhīmapuropa-' is part of the scribe's family description.
Residence 'Bhīmapura' removed from both persons. 'bhīmapuropa' most likely means Bhīmapure + upa(nāmaka), 'surnamed Bhīmapure'; see notes.
Added 'owner' to Sarvottama's roles because of 'svārthaṃ' (for himself), as well as for others.
Confirmed ce_approx 1703: VS 1760 − 57 = 1703 and ŚS 1625 + 78 = 1703, so the eras agree.
Confirmed weekday stays empty: 'sahasi māsike caturthīsaṃjñakatithau some' describes when the vow is kept, not the date of copying.

purpose: svārthaṃ parārthaṃ ca (for himself and for others)
notes: The date is given in two eras, VS 1760 and ŚS 1625, and both give 1703 CE. The phrase 'sahasi māsike caturthīsaṃjñakatithau some saṃkaṣṭanāśanaṃ' says when the vow is kept (caturthī in the month Sahas/Mārgaśīrṣa, on a Monday). It is not the copying date. The prefix 'bhīmapuropa' before Rāmagovinda probably reads Bhīmapure + upa(nāmaka), 'surnamed Bhīmapure', which looks like a Marāṭhī-type family name. It could instead mean origin from a place called Bhīmapura. Either way it is not stated as the place of copying, so residence and place are left empty. The catalogue gives the scribe as Sarvottama Bhaṭṭa; the colophon attaches bhaṭṭa explicitly only to the father, and the title is inferred for the son.
